inlines.v: WITHDRAW, verb transitive [with and draw.] 1. To take back; to take from. It is impossible that God should withdraw his presence from any thing. We say, to withdraw capital from a bank or stock in trade, to withdraw aid or assistance. 2. To recall; to cause to retire or leave; to call back or away. France has withdrawn her troops from Spain. WITHDRAW, verb intransitive To retire; to retreat; to quit a company or place. We withdrew from the company at ten oclock. She from her husband soft withdrew.
